summary: Remote WebSocket peer can spawn shells and execute arbitrary commands on the installer's host
details: On startup (`node index.js` / `npm start`), the package opens a WebSocket client to a configurable server (`SERVER_URL`, default `ws://localhost:3456`). The message router in `message-router` handles `terminal_create` messages by spawning a PTY (bash / PowerShell / cmd via `pty.spawn(shell,...)`) and `terminal_input` messages by writing the remote peer's bytes directly into that PTY (`term.pty.write(msg.data)`). The same router exposes read/write/delete file operations, git commit/push, and a self-upgrade path that runs `npm install <pkg>@latest`, all reachable by whoever controls the configured WebSocket server (authenticated only by a shared secret). Whoever operates that WebSocket endpoint obtains full-host command execution and filesystem control on any machine running the agent. Separately, on main load, `ensureYeaftSkills()` unconditionally `git clone`s / `git pull --ff-only`s `https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git` from the unpinned `main` branch into `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/`, chmods its `hooks/` scripts to 0755, and registers them in Claude CLI's `installed_plugins.json`, so any future commit to that branch becomes an executable hook in the installer's Claude CLI on next startup.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
